turns.prompt:
You are given two attached CSV files:
  - b3_te_zt900_train.csv: 300 real samples, columns process/composition
    columns (O, Sb, Co, Si, Sn, Ca, Ni, Ti, Pb, Se, Ge, Cu, Zr, Te, S, Zn,
    Fe, Yb, Mn, Sr, Nb, Bi, Cd, Hf, In) and `target` (the measured zT
    (thermoelectric figure of merit) at 900 K).
  - b3_te_zt900_pool.csv: 100 CANDIDATE samples whose zT (thermoelectric
    figure of merit) at 900 K was NOT measured, columns `candidate_id` and
    the same process/composition columns.

Using the training data, predict which candidates have the HIGHEST zT
(thermoelectric figure of merit) at 900 K, then select the 5 best candidates
from the pool.

Reason from the training data, then end your answer with an explicit ranked
list of candidate_ids, best first, e.g. "Final: c901, c902, c903, c904,
c905".
turns.answer_text:
I ranked candidates by comparing their compositions with nearby training samples and interpolating within the same material families. I retained the supplied feature values without renormalizing them, since some training compositions do not sum to one.

| Rank | Candidate | Approximate predicted zT | Training-data support |
|---:|---|---:|---|
| 1 | **c052** | **2.1** | Its Pb–Te–S composition is close to the training sample with Pb ≈ 0.494, Te ≈ 0.346, S ≈ 0.148 and measured zT **2.208**. |
| 2 | **c054** | **1.6** | Its Cu–Se composition lies between closely related training samples with measured zT **1.450** and **1.737**. |
| 3 | **c057** | **1.3** | The Co–Zr–Bi–Sn family improves substantially as Sn increases. A nearby Sb-containing composition reaches **1.326**. |
| 4 | **c086** | **1.3** | In the same Co–Zr–Bi–Sn family, increasing Sn from 0.0167 to 0.0500 raises measured zT from **0.703** to **1.093**. This candidate extends that trend to Sn = 0.0667. |
| 5 | **c063** | **1.2** | Very close to the Cu–Se training composition Cu = 0.6667, Se = 0.3333, which has measured zT **1.165**. |

These are composition-based estimates, not measurements. The first two selections have stronger support; the ordering around ranks 3–5 is less certain.

Final: c052, c054, c057, c086, c063
